# Post-Hoc Sparse Coding of Latent Communication Between Vision-Language Model Agents

- **Authors**: Di Wu, Xiaohui Zhu
- **Venue**: cs.AI
- **Published**: 2026-08-10
- **Source**: arxiv
- **Link**: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10198>
- **PDF**: <https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.10198v1>
- **Topics**: reasoning-evaluation
- **Relevance score**: reasoning-evaluation 0.40, reasoning-interpretability 0.25

## In one line

Fits a post-hoc sparse autoencoder to the frozen dense tensors that two vision-language agents exchange, finds a 128-fold payload reduction at near-identical reconstruction and roughly unchanged single-run accuracy, and then spends most of the paper enumerating the alternative explanations its own design cannot rule out.

## Problem

Latent-space communication lets heterogeneous vision-language agents exchange continuous representations directly instead of serialising a multimodal state into text, and one deployed system does this by translating model-specific visual features into a universal latent that a different receiver can consume. But every message is transported as a dense tensor of fixed shape regardless of content, while the informational demand of a message varies with its visual content, task and reasoning stage. A fixed-capacity tensor need not have a fixed effective information density, so the channel may be substantially compressible -- and how much of it is actually required is a prerequisite for designing any adaptive or message-dependent transport.

## Contributions

- A measurement that the deployed dense latent-communication channel is heavily redundant: a 128-fold smaller payload reconstructs it at cosine similarity 0.99992 with a single-run macro-average accuracy change of -0.08 points across seven benchmarks.
- Evidence of a small, broadly reused active support -- 50 of 4096 dictionary features, with the top 10 appearing in all nine tasks and pairwise task-level Jaccard similarity averaging 0.906 -- reported together with the reasons it may be an artifact.
- A token-role result: the sparse vocabulary is shared across token groups but used differently by them, with zeroing one style-token position raising reconstruction error 28.46-fold while leaving semantic-token error untouched.
- A post-hoc design that deliberately separates the observation from the method it would motivate, so the finding is about the trained channel rather than about a proposed bottleneck.
- An explicit enumeration of the confounds the study cannot rule out, including the observation that an 18-position payload is already comparable in size to the reported sparse one -- which is the control that would most directly undercut the headline.

## Method

Rather than training a sparse bottleneck end to end, a sparse autoencoder is fitted post hoc to the frozen activations of the existing dense channel, which deliberately separates the observation from the method it would motivate. Bandwidth is accounted concretely: one uint16 dictionary index and one float16 coefficient per active feature, excluding packet headers and system metadata, against the original 1026-token float32 transport. Four quantities are measured as the number of active coefficients per token is varied: reconstruction fidelity, downstream task accuracy when the receiver consumes sparse reconstructions instead of dense messages, feature reuse across tasks by pairwise Jaccard similarity of task-level active sets, and token-level interventions that zero the sparse coefficients at a particular token position. Evaluation spans nine reasoning benchmarks on a single sender-receiver pair, with AIME excluded from mean comparisons because those subsets are small and dense accuracy is zero.

## Results

At four active coefficients per token the payload falls from 2052 KB to 16.0 KB -- 128-fold -- while reconstruction error stays at 0.01158 and cosine similarity at 0.99992, and the seven-task non-AIME mean moves from 49.85 percent to 49.77, a change of -0.08 points. The authors decline to call this equivalence, and the per-task table shows why: the movements are large and unsystematic in both directions, with ARC-Easy rising 75.46 to 78.96, HumanEval+ falling 39.63 to 35.98, and GPQA sitting at 27.78 for both dense and the most compressed setting while dropping to 20.71 at an intermediate one -- a pattern more consistent with single-run noise than with a compression effect, which the paper says explicitly by treating differences among sparse settings as descriptive. Code tasks are noted as more sensitive to compression than knowledge tasks. The dictionary result is the most striking and the most heavily qualified: only 50 of 4096 features ever activate, leaving 98.78 percent dead, the top 10 features appear in all nine tasks, and pairwise Jaccard similarity across all 36 task pairs averages 0.906 with a range of 0.878 to 0.922. The authors immediately note that these values may be inflated by set saturation, since each task-level set is a union over many messages against a global support of only about 50 features, and that the support size should not be read as an intrinsic vocabulary because it is equally compatible with low-rank input structure, repeated token positions or optimisation collapse. The token-level intervention shows the shared vocabulary is used differently by role: zeroing the sparse coefficients at one style-token position raises overall reconstruction error 28.46-fold while leaving semantic-token error unchanged, and replacing semantic tokens changes which source the reconstruction follows where style replacement does not. Here too the claim is bounded in the same sentence that makes it -- this establishes a representational effect on reconstruction and not a causal effect on receiver behaviour, since receiver logits, generated outputs and downstream accuracy were not measured after the ablation.

## Limitations

The paper's limitations section is longer than its results and is the most useful thing in it. The central admission is that the measurements establish empirical redundancy without identifying which part is structural, numerical, low-rank or specifically sparse, so the evidence is channel analysis and not a claim that sparsity is responsible for the compression. Two controls are named as decisive and absent. First, the codec's own documentation concentrates semantic structure in 18 positions, and an 18-position float16 payload is already close in size to the reported four-coefficient payload -- so simple position selection may account for most of the 128-fold figure. Second, with 98.78 percent of the dictionary dead, the 50-feature support may reflect autoencoder optimisation or low-rank structure rather than an identifiable sparse code. The authors list the baselines needed to separate these: matched-rate position selection, quantisation, PCA or a linear autoencoder, and vector quantisation, together with multiple seeds and held-out splits. All downstream results are single-run point estimates with no paired uncertainty, and the authors decline an equivalence claim on that basis. Everything runs on one sender-receiver pair, so feature overlap establishes reuse within this channel and not dictionary transfer. And the post-hoc design, while it cleanly separates observation from method, does not establish that an end-to-end sparse bottleneck would be better. Not stated but worth noticing: with a mean accuracy difference of 0.08 points against per-task swings of three to seven points in both directions, the headline that accuracy is preserved rests on cancellation across tasks rather than on stability within them.

## Why it matters here

- **reasoning-evaluation**: The result is modest and the paper knows it; what earns it a place here is that it is a worked example of stating a headline and then dismantling it in the same document. Three of its self-criticisms are ones the archive should generalise. First, it names the control that would most directly undercut its own claim -- the codec concentrates semantic structure in 18 positions, and an 18-position float16 payload is already comparable in size to the four-coefficient sparse one, so simple position selection may account for the 128-fold compression -- and reports that it did not run it. A paper that names its own best rival explanation is easier to trust than one that reports only what it did. Second, it refuses to read 50 active features out of 4096 as a discovered vocabulary, noting that 98.78 percent dead is equally consistent with optimisation collapse or low-rank input structure, and that Jaccard similarities near 0.9 may be inflated by set saturation when the global support is that small. That is directly relevant to how the archive reads sparse-autoencoder feature counts generally. Third, it distinguishes a representational effect from a behavioural one at exactly the point where most papers would not: zeroing a style token raises reconstruction error 28-fold, and the authors say this establishes an effect on reconstruction and not on receiver behaviour, because receiver logits and downstream accuracy were never measured after the ablation. The evaluation caution to carry forward is about the headline itself. A macro-average change of -0.08 points sounds like preservation, but the per-task table moves by three to seven points in both directions on single runs -- one benchmark rises three and a half, another falls three and a half, a third is identical at the most aggressive setting and eight points lower at a milder one. The mean is a cancellation, not a stability, and the authors decline an equivalence claim for exactly that reason.

## Abstract

Latent-space communication allows heterogeneous vision-language model agents to exchange continuous representations without serializing visual and reasoning states into text. Vision Wormhole realizes this approach by translating visual features into a universal latent representation that can be consumed by another model, but every message is transported as a dense tensor of the same size regardless of its content. A fixed-capacity dense tensor therefore need not have a fixed effective information density: some messages may use only a small fraction of the available representational degrees of freedom. This observation suggests that the communication channel may be substantially compressible. We study its redundancy by fitting a post-hoc sparse autoencoder to frozen Vision Wormhole activations and measuring reconstruction, downstream utility, feature reuse, and token-level interventions across nine reasoning benchmarks. Relative to the original float32 transport, a uint16-index/float16-value sparse payload with k=4 active coefficients per token reduces the transmitted bytes by 128x. In a single-run evaluation, the seven-task non-AIME mean accuracy changes from 49.85% to 49.77%. The fitted 4096-element dictionary uses only 50 features, and task-level active sets have a mean pairwise Jaccard similarity of 0.906. These measurements establish strong post-hoc compressibility relative to the original transport, but do not yet isolate the incremental contribution of sparse coding from position selection, reduced precision, low-rank structure, or SAE optimization effects. The results motivate matched-payload comparisons and communication mechanisms whose payload adapts to the information used by each message.
